newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Brash says RBNZ won't accept inflation near 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brash says RBNZ won't accept inflation near 3 pct.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said in a letter to the New Zealand Herald editor published on Monday that the bank will not accept underlying annual inflation "on or just under 3 percent any more than it will be comfortable with underlying annual inflation tracking at about zero".
"I want the markets and all price setters to be very clear about that," Brash said.
Brash was replying to a column by Infometrics Economist Gareth Morgan titled "More than economics" which Brash said cast doubt on the Reserve Bank's commitment to price stability.
Brash repeated comments that the bank had not gone soft on inflation and would be striving to keep the rate "well inside" the 0-3 percent target range.
"We best do that by trying to have underlying annual inflation as close to the middle part of the range as possible and, yes, the mid-point of the target range is 1.5 percent," he said.
